items.claim: The row's rejected rival (the succession verse web:Dan.5.31 = oshb:Dan.6.1 standing alone as a notice) is turned down partly because no mark follows that verse. The silence is real, but a missing mark is not evidence against a rival; only the dependence of the appointments on the succession verse is a text reason. The span itself is a coherent setting unit and its boundaries stand.
items.both_sides: Onset seam: before it, 5:30 reports the king's death under the in-that-night formula and a PE follows 5:30 (WLC only); after it, web:Dan.5.31 = oshb:Dan.6.1 opens with a conjoined subject-first clause naming Darius the Mede, which the bare name Darius in web:Dan.6.1 = oshb:Dan.6.2 presupposes. Close seam: web:Dan.6.3 = oshb:Dan.6.4 ends on the king's intention to promote Daniel; web:Dan.6.4 = oshb:Dan.6.5 turns to the officials as agents. Both web:Dan.6.3 = oshb:Dan.6.4 and web:Dan.6.4 = oshb:Dan.6.5 open with the weak connective, so the connective favours neither side and the close rests on the change of agent alone. Medium-low is the right grade.

suggested_fix.fact: The one-verse rival is rejected on the text alone: the appointments that follow depend on the succession verse for their king. The absence of a mark after that verse is a single-witness silence to disclose, not a reason.

evidence: MEASURED (mark layer, WLC only): marks in the span of this cluster stand after oshb:Dan.5.30 (PE), oshb:Dan.6.6 (SAMEKH), oshb:Dan.6.11 (SAMEKH) and oshb:Dan.6.29 (PE); none after oshb:Dan.6.1. The row's absence claim is true; its use as a ground of rejection is the defect.

Second finding, low (triage, boundary_rationale): two layer-held facts carry no tier word: the PE after 5:30 (held by the mark layer) and the weak connective opening web:Dan.6.4 = oshb:Dan.6.5 (held by the device inventory, then_aram at oshb:Dan.6.5). Both are true as checked; each owes EXTRACTED with its layer.

Third finding, low (undisclosed device): the device inventory also lists then_aram at oshb:Dan.6.4, the row's own close verse (web:Dan.6.3 = oshb:Dan.6.4). The rationale names the connective only on the far side, which makes the far side look more marked than the near side; the two are formally alike.

Fourth finding, low (device_notes): the sentence on the note layer (an anomalous-form note and a ketiv/qere adjustment note at web:Dan.5.31 = oshb:Dan.6.1) is true of the mark layer's other-notes entry for oshb:Dan.6.1 but carries no tier word in that field; the K/Q table itself has no entry for oshb:Dan.6.1, so the wording should keep these as editorial notes, not as a K/Q reading.

Checked and sound: the Aramaic quotation in device_notes is an exact prefix of oshb:Dan.6.1; language A for every verse oshb:Dan.6.1 to oshb:Dan.6.29 (language-zone layer); zone duals present on every in-zone ref; no run of five consecutive WEB words in the prose fields; unit_type narrative fits (no speech in the span).

items.claim: The plot and the interdict (web:Dan.6.4 = oshb:Dan.6.5 through web:Dan.6.9 = oshb:Dan.6.10) form one movement: the officials seek a ground, agree on one, petition the king, and the king signs. The onset rests on the change of agent and the close on the signing; medium-low is honest because both edges rest on content and weak connectives.
items.both_sides: Onset: web:Dan.6.3 = oshb:Dan.6.4 closes on the king's plan for Daniel; web:Dan.6.4 = oshb:Dan.6.5 makes the officials the subject. Close: web:Dan.6.9 = oshb:Dan.6.10 has the king sign, introduced by the because-of-this connective (device inventory, oshb:Dan.6.10); web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11 opens with a fronted subject, Daniel, and a when-clause, not with the weak connective. The far side of the close is the better marked of the two sides.
evidence: MEASURED: SAMEKH after oshb:Dan.6.6 and paseq once in oshb:Dan.6.8 (mark layer, WLC only), both disclosed by the row; no K/Q entry in oshb:Dan.6.5 to oshb:Dan.6.10, and the row claims none.

EXTRACTED (device inventory): then_aram at oshb:Dan.6.5, 6.6 and 6.7; o_king_live_forever_aram at oshb:Dan.6.7; because_of_this_aram at oshb:Dan.6.10. The row's device claims hold. The Aramaic quotation is an exact prefix of oshb:Dan.6.5.

Finding, low (triage, boundary_rationale): the two connective facts (then_aram at web:Dan.6.4 = oshb:Dan.6.5, because_of_this_aram at web:Dan.6.9 = oshb:Dan.6.10) are layer-held and carry no tier word; they owe EXTRACTED with the device inventory. No count stands in the field.

Finding, low (undisclosed text signal bearing on the stated rival): the verb הַרְגִּ֖שׁוּ stands in exactly three verses of the book, oshb:Dan.6.7, oshb:Dan.6.12 and oshb:Dan.6.16 (MEASURED, consonantal scan of the witness), each time as the officials move on the king or on Daniel. Its first occurrence opens web:Dan.6.6 = oshb:Dan.6.7, the verse straight after the SAMEKH. The rival cut the row rejects therefore has a text signal on its onset side as well as the mark; the rejection (the petition carries out the plan) still holds, but the rival is stronger than stated and should be said to stay live.

Note on unit_type: speech fills web:Dan.6.5 = oshb:Dan.6.6 through web:Dan.6.8 = oshb:Dan.6.9 and the king answers by an act, not a speech. The type dialogue is defensible by weight of speech; the two-sided exchange at the den is typed narrative three rows on, so the pair is not typed by one rule. Left to the end review.

items.claim: The device inventory labels its blessed_aram hit at oshb:Dan.6.11 (web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11) as the homograph for kneeling, not blessing. The row lists blessed_aram as a signal 'in the prayer verse' and as a tag without that label, so it presents a blessing formula the verse does not hold.
items.both_sides: The boundaries stand. Onset: web:Dan.6.9 = oshb:Dan.6.10 ends the conspiracy with the signing; web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11 opens with Daniel as fronted subject and a when-clause, and it does not open with the weak connective. Against the onset: web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11 ends on a habitual clause (he did as before), a SAMEKH follows it, and web:Dan.6.11 = oshb:Dan.6.12 opens with the weak connective plus the assembling verb, so the prayer verse can also be read as the close of the interdict unit. Close: web:Dan.6.15 = oshb:Dan.6.16 is the officials' last speech, again opened by the assembling verb; web:Dan.6.16 = oshb:Dan.6.17 is the king's command and the casting. Medium-low is right for both edges.

suggested_fix.fact: The inventory's hit in this verse is the verb for kneeling (he knelt on his knees); the verse holds prayer and thanksgiving but no blessing formula, and the tag is kept only with that label.

evidence: EXTRACTED (device inventory, formulae.blessed_aram.homograph_note): the entry says the oshb:Dan.6.11 match is the verb 'he knelt' and not 'bless', kept and labelled. MEASURED on the witness: oshb:Dan.6.11 reads בָּרֵ֣ךְ עַל בִּרְכ֗וֹהִי at words 19 to 21 of the verse.

Second finding, medium (strongest rival misstated): strongest_rejected_alternative frames the SAMEKH after web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11 as leaving the prayer a one-verse unit. That consequence follows only from the row's own onset. The stronger rival is web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11 as the CLOSE of the preceding unit, with the next unit opening at web:Dan.6.11 = oshb:Dan.6.12: the two SAMEKH marks of the tale stand after oshb:Dan.6.6 and oshb:Dan.6.11 (MEASURED, mark layer, WLC only), and the verse after each opens a move of the officials with the verb הַרְגִּ֖שׁוּ (oshb:Dan.6.7 and oshb:Dan.6.12; the third and last occurrence is oshb:Dan.6.16; MEASURED, consonantal scan of the witness). Mark and text signal agree twice. INFERRED weighing: the row's cut is still defensible on the fronted subject at web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11, so the decision is to name this rival and say it stays live, not to move the seam.

Third finding, low: device_notes ends with a statement that the king works until sunset to save Daniel and fails. The first half is in web:Dan.6.14 = oshb:Dan.6.15 (WEB); 'fails' is a reading of web:Dan.6.15 = oshb:Dan.6.16 and web:Dan.6.16 = oshb:Dan.6.17 and carries no tier; it owes INFERRED.

Fourth finding, low: the tags name answered_and_said; the inventory's keys are answered_and_said_aram_strict (oshb:Dan.6.13) and answered_and_said_aram_loose (oshb:Dan.6.13 and 6.14). The fact holds; the key is not the inventory's.

Checked and sound: SAMEKH after oshb:Dan.6.11 and paseq once in that verse disclosed; K/Q once at oshb:Dan.6.14 disclosed; the INFERRED word on the onset clause is not too strong (the inventory's then_aram list omits oshb:Dan.6.11); the Aramaic quotation is an exact prefix of oshb:Dan.6.11; no five-word WEB run.

items.claim: The casting, the sealing and the king's sleepless night (web:Dan.6.16 = oshb:Dan.6.17 through web:Dan.6.18 = oshb:Dan.6.19) hold together as the execution of the sentence, and the close falls on a real shift of time: night in web:Dan.6.18 = oshb:Dan.6.19, first light in web:Dan.6.19 = oshb:Dan.6.20. Medium-low fits an edge resting on a time shift between two verses that both open with the weak connective.
items.both_sides: Onset: web:Dan.6.15 = oshb:Dan.6.16 is the officials' ultimatum in speech; web:Dan.6.16 = oshb:Dan.6.17 is the king's command and its execution. Close: web:Dan.6.18 = oshb:Dan.6.19 takes the king to his palace for the night; web:Dan.6.19 = oshb:Dan.6.20 brings him out at dawn. The device inventory lists then_aram at oshb:Dan.6.19 and oshb:Dan.6.20 alike, so the connective is neutral and the time words carry the edge.
evidence: MEASURED (mark layer, WLC only): no mark after oshb:Dan.6.16 and none after oshb:Dan.6.19, so the row's statement of no mark on either seam is true; the row uses the silence as a disclosure and a reason for the lower grade, not as counter-evidence. K/Q once at oshb:Dan.6.17, disclosed.
EXTRACTED (device inventory): then_aram and answered_and_said (strict and loose) at oshb:Dan.6.17. The Aramaic quotation is an exact prefix of oshb:Dan.6.17.

Finding, low (triage, strongest_rejected_alternative): the count 'nine verses' is true (web:Dan.6.16 = oshb:Dan.6.17 through web:Dan.6.24 = oshb:Dan.6.25 is nine verses, MEASURED by subtraction) but carries no tier; the ground of rejection is a weighing and owes INFERRED.

Note: the rival named is the strongest one. A second rival, the night verse web:Dan.6.18 = oshb:Dan.6.19 opening the vigil-and-dawn sequence with the king as subject, is weaker because the dawn verse supplies the time shift, and it need not be added.

items.claim: The dawn scene (web:Dan.6.19 = oshb:Dan.6.20 through web:Dan.6.24 = oshb:Dan.6.25) is one movement from the king's question through the rescue to the retribution, and its close falls where narration gives way to the king's letter at web:Dan.6.25 = oshb:Dan.6.26. Medium-low is honest: the onset rests on a time shift and the close on a change of form across a verse that itself opens with the weak connective.
items.both_sides: Onset: night and sleeplessness in web:Dan.6.18 = oshb:Dan.6.19; dawn and haste in web:Dan.6.19 = oshb:Dan.6.20. Close: web:Dan.6.24 = oshb:Dan.6.25 ends the reversal with the accusers destroyed; web:Dan.6.25 = oshb:Dan.6.26 carries the address to every people and the peace greeting, which the device inventory lists at oshb:Dan.6.26. The far side of the close holds formulas; the near side holds none, so the edge is carried from the far side.
evidence: EXTRACTED (device inventory): living_god_aram at oshb:Dan.6.21; o_king_live_forever_aram at oshb:Dan.6.22; then_aram at oshb:Dan.6.20, 6.22 and 6.24. The row's device claims and its EXTRACTED tier in device_notes hold.
MEASURED (mark layer, WLC only): K/Q once at oshb:Dan.6.21 and once at oshb:Dan.6.23, both disclosed; no PE or SAMEKH in or at the edge of the span, and the row claims none.

Finding, low (triage, boundary_rationale): the weak connective at web:Dan.6.19 = oshb:Dan.6.20 is a layer-held fact with no tier word (owes EXTRACTED, device inventory), and 'a genre shift from narration to decree' is a reading with no tier (owes INFERRED). No count stands in the field.

Flag answered: the universal word flagged in boundary_rationale is the letter's own address in web:Dan.6.25 = oshb:Dan.6.26 (the WEB wording of that address is itself universal in scope); it reports the verse and is not an overclaim by the row.

The rejected rival (close at web:Dan.6.23 = oshb:Dan.6.24 with the punishment apart) is the strongest one, and its rejection is rightly tiered INFERRED. The Aramaic quotation is an exact prefix of oshb:Dan.6.20.

items.claim: The king's letter (web:Dan.6.25 = oshb:Dan.6.26 through web:Dan.6.27 = oshb:Dan.6.28) is a royal proclamation by form: address, greeting, decree clause and a doxology that ends with the deliverance from the lions. The doxology closes the letter, and the verse after it is narrator's summary. Medium fits.
items.both_sides: Onset: web:Dan.6.24 = oshb:Dan.6.25 is narrated retribution; web:Dan.6.25 = oshb:Dan.6.26 holds the address and the greeting (device inventory, oshb:Dan.6.26), though the verse begins as narration (the king wrote) under the weak connective, so the letter proper starts inside the verse. Close: the doxology runs to the end of web:Dan.6.27 = oshb:Dan.6.28; web:Dan.6.28 = oshb:Dan.6.29 opens with a conjoined subject-first clause on Daniel in the narrator's voice. No mark stands after oshb:Dan.6.28 (MEASURED, WLC only), so this edge rests on form and voice alone.
evidence: EXTRACTED (device inventory): to_all_peoples_nations_tongues_aram and peace_be_multiplied_aram at oshb:Dan.6.26; decree_aram and living_god_aram at oshb:Dan.6.27; then_aram at oshb:Dan.6.26. The row's claims and tiers hold.
MEASURED (mark layer, WLC only): K/Q once at oshb:Dan.6.26 and once at oshb:Dan.6.27; paseq twice in oshb:Dan.6.27; all disclosed.

Finding, low (triage, strongest_rejected_alternative): no count stands in the field; the ground (the notice is the narrator's and not the king's) is a reading of web:Dan.6.28 = oshb:Dan.6.29 against web:Dan.6.27 = oshb:Dan.6.28 and carries no tier; it owes INFERRED.

Finding, low: the rationale says 'formula on both seams'. Formulas stand at the onset and inside the close side; the far side of the close (web:Dan.6.28 = oshb:Dan.6.29) holds no inventory formula. The edge is real but is carried by voice and clause form there.
The rival named (absorbing the closing notice) is the strongest one for a three-verse letter. The Aramaic quotation is an exact prefix of oshb:Dan.6.26.

items.claim: The grade high is argued from the close alone. The row's onset edge, between the end of the doxology in web:Dan.6.27 = oshb:Dan.6.28 and the notice in web:Dan.6.28 = oshb:Dan.6.29, is the same edge the preceding row grades medium from its side; it has no mark and no formula on the notice side. A one-verse row cannot stand higher than its weaker edge, and this is the only high in the book's 75 rows.
items.both_sides: Onset edge: close side, the letter's doxology ends in web:Dan.6.27 = oshb:Dan.6.28; onset side, web:Dan.6.28 = oshb:Dan.6.29 opens with a conjoined subject-first clause on Daniel in the narrator's voice; no mark after oshb:Dan.6.28. That is a real edge resting on voice and clause form, of medium strength. Close edge: web:Dan.6.28 = oshb:Dan.6.29 is a regnal summary naming two reigns; a PE follows oshb:Dan.6.29 (WLC only); 7:1 opens with a dateline that restarts the regnal sequence. That edge is as strong as any in the book. The unit and both boundaries stand; only the grade moves.

suggested_fix.fact: The grade answers to both edges of the notice: the close is strong (regnal summary, then a dateline), and the onset rests on the change from the king's voice to the narrator's with no mark, the same edge the letter's row grades medium.

evidence: MEASURED over the rows file: confidence 'high' stands on this row only; the row before it (the letter) carries medium for the shared edge.

MEASURED (mark layer, WLC only): PE after oshb:Dan.6.29; no mark after oshb:Dan.6.28; K/Q once at oshb:Dan.6.29 (on the last word, not in the words the row quotes). EXTRACTED (device inventory): oshb:Dan.7.1 is a dateline entry with the numeral for 'one'. The row's close-side claims and tiers are true.

Second finding, low: the rationale counts the PE as one of 'two independent device classes' that raise the grade. A mark of one witness informs and does not decide, so the grade should rest on the regnal summary and the dateline; the PE is disclosure.

Third finding, low (triage, strongest_rejected_alternative): 'two reigns' is a count with no tier; it is true of web:Dan.6.28 = oshb:Dan.6.29 (WEB names Darius and Cyrus) and owes EXTRACTED. The voice claim is a reading and owes INFERRED.
Fourth finding, low (triage, device_notes): the K/Q statement names its layer but carries no tier word; it is true and owes EXTRACTED.

Checked and sound: unit_type summary_notice fits; a one-verse row is allowed for this type; the Aramaic quotation is an exact prefix of oshb:Dan.6.29; 7:1 lies outside the numbering zones and needs no dual.

W3-009 boundary_rationale: the weak connective at web:Dan.6.4 = oshb:Dan.6.5 and the because-of-this connective at web:Dan.6.9 = oshb:Dan.6.10 (layer facts, no tier); no count. unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether a row's grade is bound by its weaker edge. The rule is stated in one row of the next writer part and not in the strategy, which says only that a grade is never rounded up.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The W3-014 challenge rests on it; if a notice row is graded on its close alone, high could stand and the item falls to a note.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the thrice-used assembling verb (oshb:Dan.6.7, 6.12, 6.16) should count as an onset signal in this tale. It is not in the device inventory; I measured it on the witness only.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: It lines up with both SAMEKH marks and supports a rival tiling (web:Dan.6.4 = oshb:Dan.6.5 to web:Dan.6.5 = oshb:Dan.6.6; web:Dan.6.6 = oshb:Dan.6.7 to web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11; web:Dan.6.11 = oshb:Dan.6.12 onward) against the rows' cuts at web:Dan.6.4 = oshb:Dan.6.5 and web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11. I judged the rows' cuts defensible and asked only that the rival be named; an end review may weigh it differently.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The typing of speech-heavy rows: W3-009 is dialogue with a one-sided speech, W3-012 is narrative with a two-sided exchange.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The closed vocabulary defines dialogue as an exchange between parties; the two rows are not typed by one rule, and a class ruling would settle both.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The parent-level rival that web:Dan.5.31 = oshb:Dan.6.1 closes the Belshazzar tale as the fulfilment of 5:28 was not re-argued here; rows may not straddle a parent seam.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: If the end review moves that seam, W3-008 loses its first verse and its onset must be re-argued from web:Dan.6.1 = oshb:Dan.6.2.
